pf.license.who_holds: The business holds the pet transport license. Each driver needs a valid driver's license: the business's own check.

pf.license.background_checks: Drivers: the business's own check of the driver's license and record, or as the state's rules require.
pf.license.not_this_work: Emergency vet transport, pet relocation by air or across states, boarding, grooming and dog walking are other kinds of work, with their own plug-ins.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: a driver picks the pet up at the customer's door and takes it to the vet, groomer, daycare or another address, then back. Depot runs start and end at the business's own depot.

pf.services.capacity: Door to door: up to 3 pets of one household per trip, each in its own crate or carrier, or clipped into a safety harness. Depot runs: up to 6 crates a van.
pf.services.nobody_home: No. An adult hands the pet over at the door and takes it back. A pet is never taken from an empty home, and never from a child alone.
pf.services.not_offered: Emergency vet transport (call the vet or an emergency service), flights and moves across states, rides over 60 miles, pets over 100 lb, wildlife, livestock, venomous pets and puppies under 8 weeks. A pet that has bitten a person rides only if the owner OKs it, crated and muzzled.

what_happens: A pet hurt, very sick, overheating or poisoned now: a pet taxi is not an emergency ride, and Rosie can't judge how sick a pet is. It says to call the vet, or the nearest 24-hour emergency vet, now. No booking until the pet is safe.
A person bitten and hurt: call 911 first.
A pet lost right now: Rosie gives the business's number to call, and tells the owner at once.
Signs of a catching illness: no depot run until a vet clears the pet. A door-to-door trip to the vet can still be booked, and the customer tells the clinic.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for an emergency now. Yes, after the owner's OK, for a pet that has bitten. Door-to-door only, for a pet not cleared for the shared van.

pf.first_steps.plan: A weekly plan, like daycare runs every Monday and Wednesday, gets its own yes, apart from the booking, and its terms are texted back. If the first ride shows the pet can't ride safely, the plan ends with nothing charged.

pf.visit.check_in: At the door: the customer gives the check-in code to the driver, who takes the crate or carrier. At the depot: the code is given at drop-off, and again at pick-up. DONE with a photo of the pet at the destination confirms the ride.
pf.visit.entry_codes: Gate or building codes are shown only to the driver on the job, on the ride day. Each use is logged. Deleted 72 hours after the plan ends.
pf.visit.handover: The pet goes to an adult named on the booking, at both ends. Someone else is asked for the code first. A child alone doesn't hand a pet over.
pf.visit.ride_report: Pick-up time, drop-off time, the crate or harness checked, any notes, and a photo at the destination.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: An extra stop, an extra pet or more wait time only when the customer says yes by text first, priced from the list. It is paid with the ride.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE with the drop-off time and a photo at the destination.
pf.visit.weather: Heat over the owner's limit, ice, deep snow or a storm: the ride moves to a safer time, no fee, or the customer cancels free. A pet is never left alone in a parked vehicle.

pf.money.start: Door to door: a card saved at booking, and the ride charged to it at DONE. A vet round trip, or any ride booked around a vet appointment, is paid in full when booked. A long-distance trip takes a $40 deposit when booked, and the rest is charged to the saved card at DONE. Sam can send a bill after the ride instead. Depot runs: a daycare run saves a card and is charged at pick-up; a hospital run is paid in full when booked. The crate fit check is free.
pf.money.deposits: A deposit only for a long-distance trip (the example: $40), taken when booked, with the rest charged at DONE. Nothing is held.
pf.money.fees: A late cancel (the example: inside 2 hours before pick-up; at the depot, inside 24 hours) or a no-show: up to $25 (depot: $20), never more than what was paid, and only if the owner confirms. No answer, no fee. At the door, the driver waits 15 minutes for an adult, then leaves. A change the business makes never costs the customer.
pf.money.plans: Each plan ride is charged at its own DONE, or billed after by text. Rosfield's $2 counts once a month for a plan.
pf.money.tips: Optional, all to the driver. A tip line only if the owner turns it on.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes pet transport, from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking, once a month for a plan.

pf.rules.local_rules: Vehicle, carrier and animal transport rules, as the state's or city's form sets them.

matter_most: A pet gets loose at a stop: the owner and the customer are told at once. The business handles it; Rosie never admits fault or offers money.
A pet is unwell on the ride: the driver pulls over, texts, and takes the pet to the nearest emergency vet under the vet-care OK the customer signed. The owner calls the customer.
Nobody to hand the pet over: the driver waits 15 minutes, then leaves; the owner decides any fee. A child alone never hands a pet over.
A driver is out: someone the customer hasn't met takes the pet only after the customer's OK. No reply: the owner calls first, or a free skip.
Weather day: heat, ice, deep snow or a storm moves the ride to a safer time, or a free cancel.
The vet runs long: extra wait time is added only after the customer's yes by text, priced from the list.
Skip, pause or end a plan. A skip after the cutoff may be charged, only if the owner confirms.
A pet not picked up at the depot on time: the owner calls the customer, then the emergency contact. A pet is never left overnight.
A vaccine record runs out: depot runs stop until a new one is on file.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.
